nodes.notes:
**Explicit supporting facts (directly quoted or paraphrased from the page text)**  

- **Name and identity**  
  - “Bruce Obomeyoma Onobrakpeya … universally acclaimed master printmaker, painter, sculptor and poet” — *Birth* section.  

- **Birth details**  
  - Born “at Agbarha‑Otor on 30th August 1932.”  

- **Early education**  
  - “After attending elementary and secondary schools in Ughelli, Sapele and Benin from 1941 to 1951, he won a Federal Government Scholarship in 1957 to the Nigerian College of Arts, Science and Technology, (now Ahmadu Bello University), Zaria where he studied and earned a Diploma in Fine Arts in 1962 and also a Postgraduate Arts Teacher's Certificate.”  

- **Teaching career**  
  - “He began his working career in 1953 as an Arts teacher at Western Boys' High School, Benin‑City. He relocated to Ondo Boys' High School in 1957.”  
  - “He was from 1963 to 1980 the Arts teacher at St. Gregory's College, Obalende, Lagos.”  

- **Residencies and positions abroad**  
  - “He became an Artist‑in‑Residence at Haystack Mountain of Art and Craft in Maine in the United States of America in 1975. He has, since then, held some of the most prestigious Art Residencies and professorship around the world, seven of which were in the United States.”  

- **University of Ibadan affiliation**  
  - “He also enjoyed the same rare privilege at the Institute of African Studies, University of Ibadan.”  

- **Annual Harmattan Workshop**  
  - “He has since 1998 organised and participated, annually, in the Harmattan Workshop for artists at Agbarha‑Otor.”  

- **Exhibitions**  
  - “In the course of his enchanting career as an artist, Onobrakpeya has held more than one hundred art exhibitions. The first of which took place in Ughelli in 1959.”  
  - Mention of exhibitions in Lagos, New York, London, Berlin, Moscow, Warsaw, Washington, Bologna, Nairobi, Illinois, Toronto, Bradford, Holland, Zurich, Bonn, Zimbabwe, Abidjan, Dakar, Dubai, etc., and a “one at the Vatican Museum in Rome in 1977.”  

- **Honours**  
  - “He received over fifty awards, honours and prizes from all over the world… in 1989 the University of Ibadan, awarded him an honorary doctor of letters.”  
  - “The Federal Government of Nigeria conferred the Member of the Order of the Federal Republic (MFR) on him in 2002.”  
  - “The United Nations Educational Scientific and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO) canonised him as a Living Human Treasure in 2006.”  

- **Publicatio‐n and corpus**  
  - “Onobrakpeya’s astonishing portfolio … includes fourteen published monographs and fourteen illustrated books.”  
  - Mentions of an “Urhobo alphabetic system he invented.”  

- **Foundation**  
  - “The Bruce Onobrakpeya Foundation (BOF) … formed in 1989.…organised the Amos Tutuola Show, Lagos (2000), the Annual Harmattan Workshop since 1998, and participated at … the Harvest of the Harmattan Retreat Exhibition organized in collaboration with the Pan African University, Lagos (2004), …”  

- **Publication dates**  
  - The page itself is dated **Friday, July 28 2017** (publication date).

| “Encouraged to use a different tool for their work during the year between the assassinations of JFK (1963) and RFK (1968)” | No mention of any tool, encouragement, or specific year. | Contradicts or fails to provide evidence. |
| “Up until 2014, they have continued to use this tool.” | No mention of continued use of any tool up to 2014. | Contradicts or no evidence. |
| “First studied at a university in Africa, then in the United Kingdom, and later in the United States.” | Studies: Ahmadu Bello University (Africa) and Haystack Mountain (USA). No mention of a UK university. | Partial evidence for Africa and USA; UK missing. |
| “Taught and held the positions of head of department and dean at the university where they studied in Africa until a year in the last decade of the 20th century.” | He taught at colleges and at University of Ibadan (Institute of African Studies), but no title of head of department or dean is indicated; no explicit end year (last decade of 20th century). | Contradicts or incomplete. |
| “Built a venue to showcase their own work as well as the work of other people.” | No mention of a venue built by the individual. Mention of exhibitions and a foundation, but no physical venue constructed by him. | Contradicts or no evidence. |
| “This venue celebrated its 25th anniversary in a year between 2015 and 2020.” | No venue anniversary mentioned. | Contradicts or no evidence. |

**Mere mentions (not tying to the question’s specific claims)**  

- The page references “Bruce Onobrakpeya Foundation” as an organization, but does not say the individual built a venue.  
- The page lists events organized by the foundation (Amos Tutuola Show, Harmattan Workshop, etc.) but none are stated as being a venue that celebrated an anniversary.  
- The page includes a brief mention that Onobrakpeya “has since 1998 organised and participated, annually, in the Harmattan Workshop for artists at Agbarha‑Otor,” but this is a workshop, not a built venue.

---

**Summary of extracted facts**

- Person: Bruce Obomeyoma Onobrakpeya.  
- Birth: 30 August 1932, Agbarha‑Otor, Nigeria.  
- Education: Diploma in Fine Arts (1962) and Postgraduate Arts Teacher's Certificate (date not specified) from Ahmadu Bello University (formerly Nigerian College of Arts, Science and Technology) in Zaria, Nigeria; Artist-in-Residence at Haystack Mountain of Art and Craft, Maine, USA (1975).  
- Teaching roles at Western Boys' High School, Benin‑City; Ondo Boys' High School; St. Gregory's College, Obalende, Lagos; Institute of African Studies, University of Ibadan.  
- Artist residencies and professorships globally, including seven in the USA.  
- Founder/administrator of the Bruce Onobrakpeya Foundation (established 1989).  
- Honors: honorary doctorate (Ibadan, 1989), MFR (2002), UNESCO Living Human Treasure (2006), numerous other awards.  
- Publications: fourteen monographs, fourteen illustrated books.  
- Notable exhibitions: over 100 worldwide, including in Vatican (1977).  
- The page is dated July 28 2017.

These facts are all directly traceable to sentences or paragraphs in the provided page text. All other claims in the question lack support or are contradicted by the text.
